operations: City of Cape Town Water and Sanitation Directorate: bulk water (catchments, dams, treatment works, bulk supply), reticulation (pump stations, reservoirs, pipelines), catchment/stormwater and scientific services branches serving c. 4.8 million residents.
scale_note: 2025/26 approved budget allocates R5bn+/3-year R18.5bn capital pipeline to water and sanitation; R127.7m-R157.5m budgeted for generators/UPS at sewer and water pump stations and treatment plants (backup power, not renewable PPA); Steenbras pumped-storage hydro (180MW) is council-owned power infrastructure, not part of W&S directorate; no wheeled solar/wind PPA identified yet for the directorate.

operations: Ekurhuleni Water Care Company (ERWAT) — municipal entity of Ekurhuleni Metro operating 19 wastewater care works across the East Rand, plus scientific/laboratory services.
scale_note: Operates 19 wastewater treatment works; company has run biogas-to-energy pilot work at its plants (anaerobic digestion) as part of its sustainability programme; no specific wheeling/solar PPA figure found on the public site as of Sep 2026.

operations: Johannesburg Water SOC Ltd — municipal entity of City of Johannesburg supplying potable water and wastewater services across Johannesburg; ERWAT (covered on its own record) handles Ekurhuleni's wastewater care separately.
scale_note: Large reticulation and pump-station network across Johannesburg metro; electricity is a major operating cost line per municipal AFS; no specific wheeling/solar PPA figure found on public site as of Sep 2026.

operations: Bundle of three water boards: Magalies Water (Rustenburg, North West, bulk water to the Bojanala/Madibeng/Rustenburg area including mining and Eskom power stations), Lepelle Northern Water (Polokwane, Limpopo) and Amatola Water (East London, Eastern Cape).
scale_note: All three remain separate, independently governed state water boards in 2026; Lepelle Northern Water and Amatola Water have both had recent governance/CEO instability (LNW CEO source dated 2022, Amatola CEO only confirmed in 2026 after a prior CEO left an incomplete term); no wheeled solar/wind PPA identified for any of the three on public sources as of research date; Magalies Water supplies bulk water into a heavy mining and Eskom power station load area on the Rustenburg platinum belt.

operations: Rand Water is Africa's largest bulk potable water utility, supplying over 18 million people across Gauteng, Free State, Mpumalanga and North West from abstraction works on the Vaal River system through treatment plants including Zuikerbosch and Vereeniging and a large reticulation network.
scale_note: Public reporting and Rand Water's own commentary describe plans to install hydropower and solar PV at its own sites and to open tenders or IPP procurement for solar PV across its value chain to reduce Eskom dependence; no single confirmed wheeling PPA figure was located on an official Rand Water page as of research date.

operations: Sedibeng Water, formerly covering Maluti-a-Phofung/Free State and parts of the Northern Cape, was disestablished in 2022/23 and its functions merged into Bloem Water; Bloem Water was itself reconstituted as Vaal Central Water, whose new 12-member board took office from 1 October 2023. The bloemwater.co.za domain now redirects to vaalcentralwater.co.za.
scale_note: Vaal Central Water supplies bulk water across the Free State and parts of the Northern Cape; a separate entity, MAP Water, was later created as Maluti-a-Phofung municipality's own water services provider, with VCW providing interim support; a CFO vacancy was still open as of March/April 2026; no wheeled solar/wind PPA identified on public sources as of research date.

operations: TCTA is the state owned financing and implementing agent for South Africa's major bulk raw water transfer schemes, principally the Lesotho Highlands Water Project and the Vaal Gauteng pipeline, raising and repaying the capital for dams, tunnels and pipelines rather than operating retail distribution.
scale_note: LHWP Phase 2 (about R40bn capex) includes the Polihali dam and reservoir and a 38km transfer tunnel, expected to deliver 400 million cubic metres per year once complete; Lesotho's Muela hydropower station (72MW, commissioned 1998) feeds Lesotho's own grid, not TCTA's operations; no wheeled solar/wind PPA identified for TCTA's own electricity supply as of research date.

operations: uMngeni-uThukela Water, formerly Umgeni Water, merged with Mhlathuze Water in 2023, is KwaZulu-Natal's bulk water board, currently planning more than R15bn of five year capex including the uMkhomazi Water Project, Lower uMkhomazi, Lower Thukela Phase 2, Greater Mpofana and Mhlabatshane bulk supply schemes.
scale_note: A 2024 CESA presentation identifies several small hydropower sites on UUW's own bulk infrastructure, the largest being the Mpofana outfall of the MMTS-2 scheme at up to 5.1MW, with other sites in the 120 to 700kW range; these remain at feasibility/business case stage, not yet built. Some remote infrastructure, such as the KwaXimba package plant, still runs on diesel gensets pending Eskom grid connection, per PMG minutes dated 17 March 2026. No wheeled solar/wind PPA identified as of research date.

operations: Vedanta Zinc International operates Black Mountain Mining, including the Gamsberg open pit zinc mine, at Aggeneys, Northern Cape, plus the Skorpion Zinc refinery in Namibia; mine water treatment plants at Black Mountain/Gamsberg manage pit dewatering and process water.
scale_note: VZI signed a PPA with Enernet Global, announced 2023 with construction from Q1 2024, for a 12MW DC solar PV plant at Black Mountain, generating roughly 29GWh per year to offset Eskom supply, under VZI's Renewables Energy Programme. A planned Phase 2 would wheel offsite solar/wind generation across the Eskom grid to Gamsberg specifically, but no signed Gamsberg wheeling PPA was found on public sources as of research date.

operations: Coega Development Corporation operates the Coega SEZ at Nelson Mandela Bay, host to the Hive Hydrogen green ammonia project (R105bn/US 5.8bn), now at front end engineering design stage (FEED, September 2025); separately the Boegoebaai green hydrogen SEZ near Port Nolloth, Northern Cape (Namakwa SEZ, designated May 2024) is being studied by Sasol as project owner.
scale_note: Hive Hydrogen's Coega project is backed by a fully permitted 1,430MW solar PV cluster, one of the largest in Hive Energy's 22-country portfolio, aiming for the lowest cost green ammonia globally. Boegoebaai remains at feasibility stage with a roughly 24-month study from September 2024 and Mizuho International sourcing co-investment partners; no FID reported yet. Coega itself reported R41bn in new investment secured and a sixth consecutive clean audit (December 2025).

operations: Sasol ecoFT is Sasol's Fischer-Tropsch based sustainable/power to liquid fuels business, producing sustainable aviation fuel at its Natref refinery (Sasol/TotalEnergies joint venture, Sasolburg) from used cooking and vegetable oil under ISCC Plus certification, alongside earlier hydrogen mobility collaboration with Anglo American Platinum and BMW.
scale_note: Natref SAF output is targeted at 1 to 2 million litres in 2026, about 16 million litres by 2027 and up to 100 million litres by 2030 (200 million litres per year group wide if Secunda is included); partnerships include White Desert (Cape Town to Antarctica SAF flights) and Sustaero's Canadian SAF project. The Sasol, Anglo American Platinum and BMW green hydrogen fuel cell pilot fleet was announced October 2023. Sasol's dedicated EVP roles for this work (Marius Brand for Sasol ecoFT/Sasol 2.0; Priscillah Mabelane for the Energy Business, departed 31 March 2024) no longer appear on Sasol's current published leadership page, suggesting the portfolio has been absorbed elsewhere in the Group Executive Committee.
